Numbers have always felt like more than numbers to me; they are the stories people and companies need to make smarter, better decisions. That curiosity about how data, trends, and storytelling come together is what drew me toward a career as a Data Analyst, where I can turn complex information into clear, actionable decisions for both businesses and my own team. I am originally from Spain, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. Across my academic and professional journey, I have completed 8 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in translating complex datasets into insights that support better decisions and measurable improvements for both the organisation and its customers.

My background has also shaped how I approach work. During my doctoral work, I had to use a method that was completely new to me; within a few weeks I was applying it confidently, and soon after that I was the person colleagues asked to walk them through it step by step. On another project, I developed a new approach to a problem my group had treated as unsolvable, and that method was later adopted by other teams. In addition, colleagues still consult me now and then when they run into questions in areas I have worked on before.

Outside of formal study, I have been drawn to the point where careful analysis meets practical impact. During one lengthy stretch of work, several setbacks threatened deadlines, and I stayed with it through each stage, adding extra hours when deadlines demanded it so that the work could still be completed properly. Through this, I have strengthened my communication, organisation, and attention to detail. I also value the shared side of data work: when I volunteered for a major undertaking outside my formal duties, I carried it alongside my regular workload for more than a year until it was completed. Looking ahead, I am eager to bring this combination of analytical curiosity, practical problem-solving, and genuine interest in clear, useful decisions to a Data Analyst role.

Clear, truthful information can change the course of a decision, whether by clarifying a story, informing someone, or helping people make better decisions. That belief is what drew me to journalism: a curiosity about people, processes, and the order of events, combined with a belief that careful reporting can make complex issues accessible and meaningful. For me, it is a profession that brings together curiosity, empathy, and public service in a way that helps communities understand the world around them. Originally from Colombia, I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100, and across my work I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes. My academic training gave me a structured way of approaching information, while my professional experience has shown me how much I value accuracy, structure, and clear communication.

That approach has been shaped by practical experience. In one role, I needed to use a new technique that the work required; within a couple of months I had learned it well enough to apply it independently in my own tasks. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, and I value those moments because they reflect the collaborative side of journalism. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when needed to bring it through to completion.

What keeps this career personal for me is how often it intersects with everyday life. One of my favourite memories is bringing a family member to a local community event I was covering, only for them to recognise someone I was interviewing from a story they had followed for years. That moment captured exactly why I want to continue in journalism: to turn complex, fast-moving information into accurate, compelling stories that readers can quickly understand and trust. I am now eager to bring that perspective, along with my academic foundation and practical experience, to a journalism role where I can contribute with clarity, care, and purpose.

That moment stayed with me because it captured the human side of engineering: the sharing of ideas, the chance to help others see practical solutions, and the chance to contribute to designs that last. Overall, I am eager to bring this combination of technical grounding, practical problem-solving, and thoughtful engineering focus to a Mechanical Engineer role.
